items.title: Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale timing weighs on Walmart's Q3 growth
items.rss_summary: US-based retail giant Walmart has said it faced a 100-basis-point headwind to its top-line growth in the third quarter as the 'Big Billion Days' sales event of its Indian e-commerce arm Flipkart shifted to the fourth quarter this year. "Timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days ("BBD") event negatively affected growth with an expected corresponding benefit to Q4," said Walmart in its earnings statement. The company saw the impact as Flipkart's 11-day Big Billion Days (BBD) festive sale shifted to a different timing compared with that of the previous year, with its sales contribution shifting to Walmart's fourth-quarter results. "As we previewed on last quarter's call, we faced a 100-basis-point headwind to top-line growth in Q3 due to the timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days event, or BBD in India, which will be reported in International's fourth-quarter results this year," said John David Rainey, Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, Walmart Inc. items.title: Rupee strengthens 17 paise to 93.15 against US dollar in early trade
items.rss_summary: The rupee appreciated 17 paise to 93.15 against the US dollar in early trade on Friday, backed by robust foreign fund flows into domestic equity markets and a retreating greenback against major rivals. Forex traders said the local unit showed resilience despite higher crude oil prices and negative sentiment in domestic stock markets. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.25 and gained further to trade at 93.15 against the greenback, up 17 paise from its previous close. On Thursday, the rupee rallied for the fourth straight session and settled 9 paise higher at 93.32 against the US dollar. In the preceding three sessions, the domestic currency gained 78 paise or 0.83 per cent since the closing level of 94.19 recorded on November 13. Anuj Choudhary from Mirae Asset Sharekhan said the rupee is expected to trade with a slight positive bias on overnight decline in crude oil prices and sharp fall in gold and silver prices, which may ease import bills. items.hinglish_title: Reliance Capital Case Me EPFO Ka ₹1,800 Crore Fasa, Vasooli Par Sawal
items.explanation: EPFO ke mutabiq insolvency process poora hone ki wajah se Reliance Capital se dues recover karne ka koi legal rasta nahi bacha hai. Sanstha ko lagbhag ₹1,800 crore ke loss ka samna karna pad raha hai. CBI dwara allegedly fund diversion ki jaanch ke chalte alag recovery options par sawal khade ho rahe hain.
